title: I’m a finance professional who vibe-coded a free multiplayer island game for friends (desktop browser)
author: Similar_Count5282
selftext:
I wanted a little online island where friends could meet, talk and do things together. That became **Akshay’s Island**.

You can explore the beach, ride boats, drive a jeep, go underwater in a submarine, or try gliding and parachuting. It’s free to play, with no microtransactions. **You’ll need a desktop or laptop—it doesn’t support mobile yet.**

I’m from a finance background, and I built this with substantial AI help and open-source resources. My part has been deciding what to build, testing it, spotting things that don’t make sense, and iterating. There’s been plenty of that last part!

The attached trailer uses actual gameplay footage, with AI assistance for editing, music and voice.

So far, I’ve spent **₹0 out of pocket**, using free tools, hosting and promotional cloud credits. It’s running on Cloudflare’s free tier, so capacity is limited.

It’s still a rough beta. I’d especially appreciate feedback on confusing controls and small features that would make playing with friends more fun without adding much graphics load.

Credits: Thanks to Dan Greenheck for open-sourcing Tidewater, and to Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI Codex / ChatGPT for helping me build and improve the game and trailer

replies.author: Similar_Count5282
replies.body:
Fair criticism—the frame rate needs work, and I can see why the video didn’t leave a good impression. This is my first attempt at game development. I come from a finance background, so I’m learning as I go with AI help.

I shared it because I was excited to get something working, but there’s clearly more to do before it feels good to play. I’m happy to open-source it if anyone wants to help improve performance or build their own, more playable version. I’d be glad to see that happen.

Thanks for being direct. If you have suggestions on where to start, I’m listening.
